title: The genus is invariant under extension
statement:
Let $C$ be a proper smooth connected curve over
$k$ and let $k\subseteq k'$ be algebraically closed. Then

$$
g(C_{k'})=g(C),
$$

compatibly with the Jacobian of
[thm-sc-jacobian-representability] (i.e. $J_{C_{k'}}\cong(J_C)_{k'}$, and the identifications of
[def-sc-jacobian] are compatible with base change).

proof.text: Hypotheses on $C$ and on $C_{k'}$. By [def-sc-curves], $C$ is a nonempty connected separated scheme of finite type and of dimension one over $k$, proper and smooth over $k$. It is projective over $k$ by [lem-sc-proper-dim-one-projective]. By [lem-sc-smooth-regular] all local rings of $C$ are domains, so distinct irreducible components of $C$ cannot meet; $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], so its finitely many irreducible components are also open, and connectedness leaves exactly one: $C$ is integral. Hence $C$ is a curve in the sense of [def-pc-curve] and a smooth projective curve in the sense of [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve]. The algebraically closed field $k$ is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed], and $C$ is nonempty and smooth over $k$, so [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] gives a point $\sigma\in C(k)$. Clause 2 of [prop-pc-xk-integral], applied to $(C,\sigma)$ and the field extension $k'/k$, shows that $C$ is geometrically integral over $k$ and that $C_{k'}$ is a smooth projective curve over $k'$, in particular integral, hence nonempty and connected. By [lem-sc-base-change-curve], $C_{k'}$ is a smooth separated proper curve over the algebraically closed field $k'$ of the same dimension one. Thus $C_{k'}$ is a proper smooth connected curve over $k'$ in the sense of [def-sc-curves]. Moreover $C_{k'}$ is geometrically integral over $k'$: for a field extension $K/k'$ one has $(C_{k'})_K=C_K$ ([def-pc-base-change], transitivity of fibre products), which is integral because $C$ is geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

The genus. By [def-sc-genus], applied to the proper smooth connected curves $C$ over $k$ and $C_{k'}$ over $k'$ (step 1), $g(C)=\dim_k H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ and $g(C_{k'})=\dim_{k'} H^1(C_{k'},\mathcal O_{C_{k'}})$. Applying the algebraically closed clause of [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent] to the proper $k$-scheme $C$, the algebraically closed fields $k\subseteq k'$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_C$, $i=1$, gives $\dim_{k'}H^1(C_{k'},\mathcal O_{C_{k'}})=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$, hence $g(C_{k'})=g(C)$.

The Jacobian. By step 1, $C$ (resp. $C_{k'}$) is a geometrically integral smooth projective curve over the separably closed field $k$ (resp. $k'$), so [thm-sc-jacobian-representability] gives Jacobians $(J_C,\varphi_C)$ and $(J_{C_{k'}},\varphi_{C_{k'}})$ in the sense of [def-sc-jacobian], and its base-change clause gives $J_{C_{k'}}\cong(J_C)_{k'}$. For the compatibility of the identifications: by [cor-pd-pic0-base-change], $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\times_kk'\cong\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C_{k'}/k'}$, where the left side is the restriction of $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ to $k'$-algebras ([def-pc-base-change]). Restricting $\varphi_C$ to $k'$-algebras and using $h_{J_C}(R)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}R,J_C)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k'}(\operatorname{Spec}R,(J_C)_{k'})=h_{(J_C)_{k'}}(R)$ for a $k'$-algebra $R$ (universal property of the fibre product) gives an isomorphism $\varphi_C\times_kk':\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C_{k'}/k'}\cong h_{(J_C)_{k'}}$. The composite $(\varphi_C\times_kk')\circ\varphi_{C_{k'}}^{-1}:h_{J_{C_{k'}}}\cong h_{(J_C)_{k'}}$ is an isomorphism of functors on $k'$-algebras, hence by the Yoneda lemma (a scheme is determined by its functor on affine schemes: *reference: Stacks Project, Schemes, [Tag 01JF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01JF)* area, elementary) it is induced by a unique isomorphism $J_{C_{k'}}\cong(J_C)_{k'}$; this is the isomorphism of the statement, and by construction it carries $\varphi_{C_{k'}}$ to the base change of $\varphi_C$, i.e. the identifications of [def-sc-jacobian] are compatible with base change.
